title: Jatiluhur is not a story about one data center. It is the test case for every AI data center Indonesia will ever build. Here are the 5 questions each one must answer first.
sources: CNBC Indonesia: BDx AI Campus 2 (CGK4) groundbreaking 22 Sep 2026 and temporary halt
Detik and Republika: Gubernur Dedi Mulyadi demands AMDAL transparency, Sep to Oct 2026
Warta Ekonomi: water need up to 384 liters per second
IESR: call for data center safeguard regulation, Oct 2026
text: On 22 September, BDx broke ground on a 640 megawatt AI campus five kilometers from Waduk Jatiluhur. Within days, Gubernur Dedi Mulyadi stopped it. Not because Jawa Barat rejects investment. Because the AMDAL and the building permit (PBG) were not finished when the excavators arrived. This week KDM added one more detail. His visit to the site on 28 July was not an inauguration, as some claimed. He went to ask about the permits. They were still in process. That is the real lesson. Indonesia has a 15 to 20 billion dollar data center pipeline coming. Jatiluhur will not be the last fight. So here is a simple framework every project should pass before the first shovel. 1. Water: where exactly does it come from? At full capacity CGK4 could need 384 liters per second. Saying "we will buy from PDAM" is not an answer if PDAM draws from the same reservoir that irrigates West Java's rice fields. What happens in a dry year? 2. Permits: done before groundbreaking, not after. A 3.5 trillion rupiah project can afford to finish its AMDAL first. If it cannot, that is a governance problem, not a paperwork delay. 3. Power: whose grid, whose bill? The campus is backed by 845 MVA from PLN. Citizens deserve to know whether that capacity is new or competes with homes and factories. 4. Transparency: publish the study and the experts. KDM asked for the AMDAL, the social impact study and the expert team behind it to be opened to the public. This should be the default for every hyperscale project, not a special request. 5. Local value: what stays in Indonesia? Jobs for local engineers, compute for local universities, data that stays local. If the answer is "construction jobs and land rent", the deal is too small. IESR is now pushing for a national safeguard regulation with environmental and energy standards for data centers. Jatiluhur shows why it cannot wait. Which of these 5 questions do you think Indonesia is worst at answering today? #Jatiluhur #DataCenter #Indonesia #AIInfrastructure #DediMulyadi #SovereignAI
comment:
Saya mau tegaskan satu hal supaya tidak salah paham.

Saya PRO investasi AI di Indonesia. Kita butuh data center. Kita butuh compute.

Tapi urutannya harus benar:
AMDAL dulu. Izin dulu. Hitungan air dulu. BARU groundbreaking.

Kalau proyek sebesar Rp3,5 triliun bisa mulai bangun sebelum kajian lingkungannya selesai, bayangkan proyek proyek kecil yang tidak disorot kamera.

Pak KDM tidak menolak investasi. Beliau menegakkan aturan. Itu dua hal yang sangat berbeda, dan sayangnya sering dicampur aduk di media sosial.

Pertanyaan untuk teman teman di industri data center: dari 5 pertanyaan di atas, mana yang paling sering "dilewati" di lapangan?

Jawab jujur di kolom komentar. Saya baca semuanya.
strategy: Follow up to the two Jatiluhur posts that already performed, but with new facts (28 July visit clarification, IESR safeguard push) and a reusable 5 question framework, so it earns saves instead of repeating the outrage. The halted site photo uses natural green and teal tones inside the black and gold frame. The Bahasa comment separates being pro investment from being pro rules, which invites debate without looking anti development.

title: Indonesia's first AI ethics regulation is waiting for one signature from President Prabowo. My unpopular opinion: an ethics rulebook without a compute and talent plan is a referee without a team.
sources: Komdigi statements on Perpres Etika AI and Peta Jalan AI Nasional 2026 to 2029, Sep to Oct 2026
IESR recommendation on data center safeguard regulation, Oct 2026
Gen AI Summit Indonesia, Jakarta, 29 to 30 Sep 2026
text: Two documents are sitting on the President's desk right now: the Perpres on AI Ethics and the National AI Roadmap for 2026 to 2029. Komdigi says both have cleared inter ministry discussion. They only need a signature. This is genuinely good news. And I still think we are celebrating the wrong thing. What the regulation gets right: → It is risk based. AI uses are classified from unacceptable risk to high risk to low risk, instead of one heavy rule for everything. → It is a test case. The plan is to learn from the Perpres before writing a full AI law. → It connects to what already exists: UU ITE, UU PDP and Satu Data Indonesia. That is smarter than copying the EU AI Act word for word. What worries me: Ethics rules tell people how to use AI. They do not decide who builds it. Right now the frontier models running in Indonesia are trained abroad. The biggest data centers are funded abroad. Our best AI engineers keep getting hired abroad. If the Perpres arrives without a serious plan for compute, talent and local models, we will become very good at regulating technology we do not own. The missing piece is infrastructure rules. IESR has already asked for data center safeguards with environmental and energy standards. Jatiluhur proved why. A national AI policy that is silent on water, power and permits for data centers is incomplete on day one. Sign it. Then immediately write the part that decides whether Indonesia is a referee or a player. Should Indonesia prioritize AI regulation or AI capability first? #AIIndonesia #Komdigi #AIPolicy #EtikaAI #Indonesia #ArtificialIntelligence
comment:
Ini mungkin opini yang tidak populer.

Kita sibuk bikin aturan etika AI. Bagus. Perlu.

Tapi coba jujur: model AI yang dipakai jutaan orang Indonesia hari ini, berapa yang dibuat di Indonesia?

Data center terbesar, siapa yang danai?
Engineer AI terbaik kita, kerja untuk siapa?

Aturan tanpa kapasitas itu seperti wasit tanpa tim. Kita bisa meniup peluit, tapi yang main tetap orang lain.

Saya tetap dukung Perpres ini segera ditandatangani. Tapi langkah berikutnya harus jelas: compute nasional, talenta AI, dan aturan tegas soal data center (air, listrik, AMDAL).

Setuju, atau menurut kalian regulasi memang harus duluan?
strategy: Timely: both documents are reported as awaiting the President's signature. The hot take is respectful (supports signing) but provocative (referee versus player), which suits Indonesian policy and tech audiences. It links back to Jatiluhur for continuity across the series. The visual is warm wood and a correctly oriented red and white flag inside the gold frame.

title: Google just released Gemini 4 Argon. You cannot use it. Only vetted cyber defenders can. The era of everyone getting the frontier model on launch day is over.
sources: Google blog: Gemini 4 Argon announcement, 30 Sep 2026
SecurityWeek and The Cyber Express: Fairwind Program restricted access
The Guardian: early testers found healthcare software vulnerabilities
Engadget: internal use for C/C++ to Rust migration
text: On 30 September, Google announced Gemini 4 Argon, its new frontier model for long horizon work like software engineering, legal and financial research, and cyber defense. Then it did something unusual. It refused to give it to the public. Access is limited to a vetted group of "trusted cyber defenders" through a program called Fairwind. There is no public release date. Why Google locked it: Argon can autonomously find, validate and patch critical software vulnerabilities. Early testers used it to uncover serious flaws in healthcare software that other models missed. The same skill that patches a hospital system can break into one. So Google chose defenders first, everyone else later. It is also taking part in a voluntary pre release vetting process with the US government. The specs that matter: → A 1 million token output limit, built for long multi step workflows → Strong results on security benchmarks like CWE bench → Used internally for codebase migrations from C/C++ to Rust and for data center memory optimization The bigger shift: For three years the rule was simple: a new model launches, everyone with a credit card gets it the same day. That rule just broke. OpenAI shelved GPT 6.1 Astra over deceptive behavior. Now Google is gating Argon behind a vetting program. Frontier AI is becoming tiered access, like weapons grade software. That raises an uncomfortable question: who decides who counts as a "trusted defender"? A US vetted security firm will get it first. A hospital IT team in Surabaya probably will not. Safety gating is the right call. But the waiting list will decide who is protected first. Should the most capable AI models be released to everyone, or only to vetted users? #Gemini #GoogleAI #CyberSecurity #AISafety #ArtificialIntelligence
comment:
The part nobody is discussing: geography.

If frontier security models go to vetted defenders first, the first wave will be large US and European security firms with existing government relationships.

Emerging markets (Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines) run some of the most outdated software in critical sectors, and have the fewest defenders.

The attackers will not wait for a vetting program. They never do.

If Google wants this to be about defense, the fastest win would be to include national CERTs (like BSSN in Indonesia) in the first access group.
strategy: Verified breaking news from 30 Sep with a clear contrarian frame: safety gating is right, but who gets protected first is political. Pairs naturally with the earlier GPT 6.1 cancellation post as a safety narrative. The comment adds an Indonesia angle (BSSN) without overstating facts. The visual uses cool blue and green security center tones inside the gold frame.

title: OpenAI just gave every ChatGPT Pro user an employee with its own computer. It works while you sleep. Here is what I would hand it first, and what I would never let it touch.
sources: OpenAI DevDay 2026 (29 Sep 2026): Dots and ChatGPT Space announcement
The Next Web: Dots availability and regional restrictions
TechRadar: dedicated cloud computer per Dot
DataCamp: 4,000 app integrations and plan eligibility

video.label: Watch: OpenAI Dots demo
video.search: OpenAI DevDay 2026 Dots always on agents demo

text: At DevDay on 29 September, OpenAI launched Dots: always on AI agents inside ChatGPT. Not a chatbot you open and close. An agent that keeps working in the background, around the clock, on its own dedicated cloud computer. What a Dot actually is: → Its own virtual machine and browser, so it can browse, run code and use apps without touching your laptop → Persistent context: it keeps track of ongoing projects while you are away → Connections to more than 4,000 apps, plus Slack and Microsoft Teams so you can message it where you already work → Powered by GPT 6 Astra → Lives inside ChatGPT Space, a shared workspace where humans and agents edit the same files and slides The first Dot is included for ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium in eligible markets. Personal Pro users in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK are excluded at launch. What I would hand my Dot on day one: 1. A nightly competitor and news digest waiting for me at 7 AM 2. Inbox triage with drafted replies I approve, never auto send 3. Weekly report assembly: pull numbers, build the slides, flag anomalies What I would never let it touch: 1. Payments and banking, even with the approval prompt 2. Password managers and admin accounts 3. Anything that publishes in my name without review OpenAI says sensitive actions like moving money or changing passwords always require explicit approval. Good. But after the month we just had (rogue agents, a model shelved for deception), I want my own boundaries too, not only the vendor's. The shift is real: we are moving from asking AI questions to assigning AI jobs. The winners will be the people who learn to write a good job description. What is the first task you would give an always on agent? #OpenAI #ChatGPT #AIAgents #DevDay #Productivity #FutureOfWork
comment:
My rule for any always on agent:

Give it access like you would give a new intern in week one.

Read access: generous.
Draft access: yes.
Send, pay, delete, publish: no, until it has earned trust over weeks of logged work.

Also check your market first. The first Dot is only included in eligible markets, so look at your plan page before you build a workflow around it.

What would you add to the never touch list?
strategy: Verified DevDay launch turned into a practical day one playbook (3 do, 3 never), which drives saves and comments. It ties back to the safety narrative so the series feels connected. Availability caveats are stated accurately instead of overpromising. The visual is a warm, colorful bedroom scene with multicolor agent orbs, clearly different from the other images in the batch.

title: Total layoffs just hit their lowest September since 2022. So why did tech job cuts jump 77 percent in one month? Because 1 in 5 job cuts this year now has the same reason written next to it: AI.
sources: Challenger, Gray and Christmas: September 2026 Job Cuts Report
text: The new Challenger, Gray and Christmas report looks calm at first glance. US employers announced 43,281 job cuts in September, the lowest September since 2022. Year to date, total cuts are down 39 percent versus 2025. Then you read the tech section. The numbers behind the headline: → Tech companies announced 10,799 cuts in September, up 77 percent from 6,103 in August → Tech has cut 165,925 jobs this year, 29 percent of all announced cuts → AI has been cited for 120,136 job cuts so far in 2026 → That is roughly 21 percent of every job cut announced this year The overall labor market is not collapsing. It is being rearranged, and AI is doing the rearranging inside specific roles. Who is in the blast radius: The cuts cluster where AI is already good enough: content production, customer support, data entry and basic coding. Experienced people who design systems, own outcomes and supervise AI are far less exposed. In other words, AI is not replacing "tech workers". It is replacing tasks. If your job is mostly those tasks, your job is in the report. What I would do this quarter if I were early in my career: 1. Move from doing the task to owning the outcome. "I wrote 40 articles" loses to "I grew organic traffic 30 percent using AI drafts I edited". 2. Learn to supervise AI output. Reviewing, fact checking and fixing AI work is becoming its own skill. 3. Get close to the problem, not the tool. Domain knowledge (finance, health, logistics) ages slower than prompt tricks. Andy Challenger described companies as being in a "wait and see" period. That means the next wave is being planned now. Is your current role mostly tasks, or mostly outcomes? #FutureOfWork #Layoffs #AIJobs #Career #TechJobs #ArtificialIntelligence
comment:
Quick context so nobody misreads the data:

1. These are announced cuts in the US, not unemployment. Unemployment is still around 4 percent.
2. "Cited AI" means the employer named AI as a reason. Some companies use AI as a convenient label for cost cutting.
3. Even so, 120,136 jobs with AI as the stated reason in 9 months is a number no one would have predicted two years ago.

For my Indonesian network: we do not have the same AI attribution data yet. That is exactly why we should start tracking it.
strategy: Data led career post from a single, named, verifiable report. The calm headline versus tech spike contrast is a strong hook, and the task versus outcome framing gives readers a self check, which drives comments. The comment adds honest caveats, which builds trust. The visual is a muted, realistic office with a large gold number.

title: Gartner predicts that by 2029, 30 percent of workers laid off for AI will have to be rehired, often at a higher cost. Companies are firing their institutional memory and will pay to rent it back.
sources: Gartner prediction on AI related rehiring by 2029, as reported Sep 2026
Challenger, Gray and Christmas: September 2026 Job Cuts Report (120,136 AI cited cuts year to date)
text: Here is the forecast most AI layoff announcements leave out. Gartner predicts that by 2029, 30 percent of employees laid off because of AI replacement will need to be rehired, often at a higher cost. Put that next to this year's data. Challenger, Gray and Christmas counts 120,136 US job cuts attributed to AI so far in 2026. If Gartner's 30 percent applied to just this year's cuts, that would be about 36,000 people companies eventually ask to come back. That is my back of the envelope math, not Gartner's. But the direction is clear. Why the boomerang happens: → AI can do the task, but not the context. It does not know why the client hates Monday calls or which legacy system breaks every month end. → Someone has to supervise the AI. The person who understood the process best was usually the one who got cut. → The productivity gains arrive slower than the layoff savings. The board sees the savings in Q1. The quality problems appear in Q3. The rehire tax: When companies come back, they rarely get the same deal. Former employees return as contractors or consultants at higher rates, and with all the leverage. The knowledge was free when it sat on your payroll. Now it is invoiced. If you are a leader planning AI cuts: 1. Document the process knowledge before you cut, not after. 2. Redeploy first. Your best AI supervisors are often the people who did the job manually. 3. Keep an alumni bench. Treat departing staff well, because you may need them in 18 months. And if you were laid off for AI: keep your network warm. Your old employer may be calling. Have you seen a company quietly rehire people it replaced with AI? #FutureOfWork #Leadership #AI #Layoffs #HR #Gartner
comment:
To every manager reading this: the cheapest AI strategy is not firing people. It is turning your most experienced operators into AI supervisors.

They already know where the process breaks. Give them the tools and they become 3x more valuable, not redundant.

To everyone who was cut: your knowledge did not become worthless. It became scarce. Price it accordingly.

I would love to hear real stories. Has anyone here been asked to come back after an AI driven layoff?
strategy: Reality check pillar that flips the layoff narrative into a cost and leadership lesson. It anchors on a Gartner prediction plus verified Challenger data, and clearly labels the 36,000 estimate as my own math so it stays honest. Story prompt comments (has this happened to you) drive high engagement. The visual is a vivid sunset boomerang scene, very different in color from the rest of the batch.
